etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
First recorded in the Edo period.
According to one theory, formed from 護摩 (goma, “a holy fire in esoteric Buddhism”) + verbalizing suffix かす (kasu), from a common fraud perpetrated in the Edo period of dressing as a monk and selling regular ash purported to be ash from such holy fires.
Alternatively, from 胡麻菓子 (goma kashi, “sesame candy”), from a particular sesame candy in the Edo period called 胡麻胴乱 (goma dōran) and notable for being a mostly empty shell.
The kanji spellings are examples of ateji. The more common spelling is in hiragana, as ごまかす.

etymologies.text: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 動(うご)く (ugoku).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 勝(か)ち (kachi, “victory, win, advantage”) + 手(て) (te, “means, way; hand”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 打(う)ち (uchi, “hitting; batting”, 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 打(う)つ (utsu, “to hit, to bat”)) + 羽(わ) (wa, “wing”). The kanji are an example of jukujikun (熟(じゅく)字(じ)訓(くん)).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Probably from Middle Chinese compound 團扇 /团扇 (dhuɑn syenᴴ, literally “circle fan”). Compare modern Mandarin 團扇／团扇 (tuánshàn).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 思(おも)い付(つ)く (omoitsuku, “to think of”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 手(て) (te, “hand”) + の (no, “-'s”, genitive particle) + 平(ひら) (hira, “flat”). Compare English flat of one's hand.

etymologies.heading: Etymology

etymologies.text: From 手(た) (ta-, “hand”) + な (na, “-'s”, archaic) + 心(こころ) (kokoro, “heart; inside”, rendaku form 心(ごころ) (gokoro)).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Compound of 生きる (ikiru, “to live, to exist”) + 甲斐 (kai, “worth, value”).
The kai changes to gai as an instance of rendaku (連濁).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 列(つら) (tsura, “row”, archaic) + 抜(ぬ)く (nuku, “to go through”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Originally referred to the (amount of) pay that a samurai in employment received and, by extension, his importance. The word consists of 貫(かん) (kan) (in its now obsolete meaning of the monetary equivalent of the income (based on crop) of a samurai) and 禄(ろく) (roku), the salary of someone in government service.
